15189.note: Big Pine Key pub known for its pizza and fish dip, in a building that started as a 1931 general store.
15189.fn: The pub's own history says the building opened in 1931 as a general store and bait shop, and the owners added a restaurant room to it in 1936.

15192.note: Lower Keys seafood restaurant at mile marker 22.5 oceanside on Cudjoe Key, with conch chowder, house smoked fish dip and Key lime pie.

15211.note: Mile marker 77.5 bayside marina with the Hungry Tarpon restaurant, boat tours and a twice-weekly Keys history tasting of conch chowder, conch fritters and Key lime pie.
15211.fn: Robbie's says it has been part of the community since 1976.

15223.note: Mile marker 81.2 roadhouse dating to 1947, serving conch chowder, conch fritters and house smoked fish dip, with a roadside barbecue stand.
15223.fn: The restaurant says it has been an Islamorada dining favorite since 1947 and a landmark on the Overseas Highway at mile marker 81.2 for over 75 years.

15224.note: Islamorada seafood restaurant serving grouper dishes, smoked fish dip and fish finished in Key lime butter.
15224.fn: The restaurant says it first opened in the Islamorada area in 1948; the year at this address was not verified.

15276.note: Open-air waterfront bar and seafood shack on Card Sound Road, a stop for bikers and boaters, known for conch fritters and live music among the mangroves.

15283.note: Key Largo seafood wholesaler, market and backyard cafe that sells stone crab claws in season and ships Keys seafood.
15283.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).
15283.fn: Key Largo Fisheries says it has supplied seafood since 1972.

15311.note: Key Largo diner serving seafood, comfort classics and Key lime pie.

15326.note: Key Largo restaurant in a house on the Overseas Highway, serving dinner nightly from 4 p.m.

15337.note: Key Largo restaurant and seafood market that buys whole fish from local commercial fishermen and fillets them on site; stone crab and lobster come in fresh off the boat in season.
15337.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).
15337.fn: The restaurant says it opened just as the Conch Republic was born (1982).

15347.note: Key Largo restaurant on the Overseas Highway, in business since 1985, serving seafood dishes and Key lime pie.
15347.fn: The restaurant says it has operated since 1985.

15356.note: Key Largo waterfront restaurant on Seaside Avenue, off the Overseas Highway, with weekend brunch.
15356.fn: Snappers was founded in 1989; it says food and drinks were served on the site as far back as the 1960s.

15390.note: Open-air Key West fish shack on Caroline Street known for its grilled or fried grouper sandwich, with live music on Friday nights.
15390.fn: Owner Buddy Owen started out selling from a wagon on Duval Street before opening this open-air shack.

15391.note: Historic Key West cafe serving breakfast through dinner daily, with oysters shucked to order, house-baked bread and fresh-squeezed juices.
15391.fn: Pepe's says it opened in 1909 and calls itself the oldest eatery in the Florida Keys; the year it moved to this Caroline Street address was not verified, so it is not counted as same-address.

15395.note: Family-friendly Key West Cuban restaurant where regulars order by number, like the No. 1 roast pork; it also has Stock Island and Marathon locations.

15407.note: Duval Street landmark bar with live music daily and a kitchen serving conch fritters, smoked fish dip and Key lime pie.
15407.fn: The bar dates its history to the end of Prohibition in 1933 and says it has been at the corner of Duval and Greene since 1937.

15470.note: Key West Cuban coffee shop with four island locations, serving café con leche, coladas, Cuban sandwiches and breakfast burritos.

15496.note: Key West shop devoted to all things Key lime, best known for slices of pie and frozen chocolate-dipped Key lime pie on a stick.

15540.note: Harborwalk oyster bar at the A&B Marina with waterfront patio seating and a daily oyster special.
15540.fn: The site's tagline says 'since 1947', but no source confirmed the oyster bar itself dates to that year.

15552.note: Key West pie shop off Duval Street making Key lime pie fresh daily from a family recipe with a handmade graham cracker crust.

15562.note: Seafood restaurant in the old Singleton Fish House and ice plant on Greene Street, where shrimpers once unloaded Key West pink shrimp.

15578.note: Waterfront seafood house and raw bar on Margaret Street; it calls itself the original Key West seafood restaurant.

15693.note: Key West restaurant at the corner of Thomas and Petronia streets serving breakfast, lunch and dinner outdoors under a Spanish lime tree.
15693.seas: Closed for vacation Sept 8 – Oct 15, 2026; otherwise open daily except Thanksgiving and Christmas.
15693.fn: The restaurant opened September 19, 1992, in a building with a century of island history.

15717.note: Key West Cuban and Conch cafe on White Street known for Cuban sandwiches pressed on fresh Cuban bread and café con leche.
15717.fn: The Keys tourism listing says Sandy's has served since 1954; the year at this address was not verified.

15748.note: Gulfside restaurant, seafood market and wholesale fishery off 35th Street in Marathon, known for its lobster Reuben and for selling stone crab claws in season.
15748.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).

15755.note: Marathon bar and grill in the 15th Street neighborhood with a wraparound balcony over Boot Key Harbor, known for its fried Key lime pie wrapped in a tortilla.

15796.note: Family- and veteran-owned Marathon fish market and eatery selling local fish, stone crab and lobster, with smoked fish spread and conch chowder.
15796.fn: It calls itself the oldest fish market and restaurant in Marathon; no founding year was given.

15806.note: Gulfside tiki diner and marina at mile marker 47.5 in Marathon, calling itself home of the original deep-fried Key lime pie, with barbecue smoked on site.
15806.fn: The restaurant describes itself as 'est. circa 1950'; no exact year was verified.

15812.note: Working-waterfront bar and grill at Safe Harbor Marina on Stock Island, known for its hogfish sandwich on Cuban bread with Swiss, onions and mushrooms.
15812.fn: The site says it has been locally owned for 23 years.

15815.note: Lower Keys roadside restaurant on the drive to Key West, serving conch fritters, fresh fish and Key lime pie with daily specials.
